news.title: Chelsea Diary: Decisive domestic action and European nights
news.body_en: A Carabao Cup trip to Anfield, European fixtures for Cobham Next Gen and Chelsea Women, and a Premier League meeting with Manchester United headline a busy seven days for the Blues. Here is everything to look out for at Chelsea this week… We begin the week by looking back at Chelsea Women's WSL victory at Crystal Palace, with highlights and reaction from Sonia Bompastor, Melvine Malard, Lexi Potter and Lucy Bronze. Attention will then turn to a packed week ahead, with both senior teams preparing for important fixtures in league and cup competitions. There will be a double helping of pre-match press conferences on Tuesday as both our head coaches look forward to midweek action. Xabi Alonso will face the media ahead of Chelsea's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie away at Liverpool, with the Blues looking to book our place in the next round of the competition. Sonia Bompastor will also speak to the media at 3pm, previewing Chelsea Women's UEFA Women's Champions League league-phase meeting with Roma. The Blues will be aiming to make home advantage count as European football returns to London. Both press conferences will be available to watch on the Chelsea Official App and website, with the latest news and key updates available across our official channels. Cobham Next Gen’s UEFA Youth League campaign begins with a trip to Estonia to play Flora Tallinn in the first leg of our round two tie. Kick-off at the Lillekula Stadium is at 5pm, with updates provided across Chelsea channels. It is also a European night for Chelsea Women as Roma visit the Cherry Red Records Stadium for a UEFA Women's Champions League encounter. Kick-off is at 5.45pm, and supporters can follow all the build-up, team news and live updates in our Chelsea Women vs Roma Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and website. We will also bring you the latest reaction and post-match coverage after the final whistle. Later in the evening, the men's team travel to Merseyside for a Carabao Cup clash with Liverpool. The tie at Anfield kicks off at 8pm, as Alonso's side look to progress in a competition that has provided plenty of memorable moments throughout Chelsea's history. The match will be broadcast live on ITV and Sky Sports in the UK. Supporters can also follow the action with minute-by-minute updates and live commentary in our Liverpool vs Chelsea Match Centre. Our focus turns to the weekend as preparations continue at Cobham. Following Wednesday's cup action, we will bring you the latest from both senior squads as the men's team prepare for Manchester United's visit to Stamford Bridge and Chelsea Women get ready for another London derby. There will also be a chance to catch up on the best of the action from our midweek fixtures, including highlights and reaction from Anfield and Chelsea Women's European encounter with Roma. Both head coaches will return to the press conference room as the weekend build-up gathers pace. Alonso will preview Saturday's Premier League meeting with Manchester United, while Bompastor will address the media at 3pm ahead of Sunday's WSL trip to Charlton Athletic. We will bring you the latest team news, the managers' thoughts and all the key talking points from both press conferences on the Chelsea Official App and website. The men's team take centre stage at Stamford Bridge as Manchester United visit for a Premier League encounter. Kick-off is at 12.30pm, with the Blues looking to bounce back in the league after the defeat to Tottenham ended our winning run. Supporters can follow all the build-up, team news and live action in our Chelsea vs Manchester United Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and website. We will provide minute-by-minute updates, live commentary and post-match reaction, alongside the best photographs and highlights from the Bridge. Earlier on Saturday, there is Academy action as Chelsea Under-18s travel to face West Ham United in the Under-18 Premier League. Kick-off is at 11am and supporters who have subscribed to CFC+ can watch the game live on our channels. We round off the week with another London derby as Chelsea Women travel to The Valley to take on Charlton Athletic in the Women's Super League. Bompastor's side kick off at 2.30pm, looking to build on their midweek European outing with a strong domestic performance against the newly-promoted hosts. The match will be shown live on BBC Two in the UK, while our Charlton Athletic vs Chelsea Women Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and website will provide all the latest team news, live updates and reaction. We will also bring you the best of the action from Saturday's meeting with Manchester United and our Under-18s' trip to West Ham, ensuring you can catch up on everything happening across the club as another busy week comes to a close.

news.title: WSL Highlights: Crystal Palace Women 1-3 Chelsea Women
WSL Full Match: Crystal Palace Women vs Chelsea Women
Melvine Malard on half-time wake-up call and love for Baltimore
news.body_en: Melvine Malard described the striker’s instinct that saw her fire in a brace in our 3-1 win against Crystal Palace on Sunday, but also explained how the team needed a jolt at half-time to spark the comeback. The Eagles took the lead from a corner after 20 minutes, which meant we trailed at half-time for the first time this season. It took just five minutes after the restart for Malard to net her first of the afternoon and then she headed in from second-half substitute Sandy Baltimore’s cross 25 minutes later. The number nine then won a penalty in the final stages of the match, which Baltimore scored to complete the 3-1 victory. With the three points successfully in the bag, Malard explained how the team reacted in the dressing room at the interval. ‘It was so good to win today because it was a hard game with the wind,’ she explained. ‘But the team could keep going and put the energy into this game. ‘We said “wake up” at half time because it wasn’t a very good start to the game, but we know our quality; we know the way we needed to play to win the game. When we came back out in the second half, we showed that quality.’ Malard shot wide of the target right before she scored from 25 yards out, and she explained how that missed opportunity spurred her on to shoot from distance. ‘I was really in the action before when I missed, and so I knew my touch was good,’ she said. ‘I told myself to shoot and that’s what I did. I am in a good place. This is a seriously good team, and we have good staff.’ Malard paid tribute to Baltimore for a superb second-half display after the pair combined on both the second and third goals against Palace. ‘I love her,’ the striker beamed. ‘She has a lot of quality to go 1-v-1, and as a striker, you only need to go in the box, and she can give you the ball. She showed that today when she came in to help the team. ‘We will take the energy we put in today to the Roma game on Wednesday. We scored three goals today, so that is good. We will keep going to score the goals.’

news.title: Sonia Bompastor on Malard 'banger' and second-half turnaround
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor explained how the weather made things difficult for Chelsea away at Crystal Palace on Sunday, but hailed the quality of French duo Melvine Malard and Sandy Baltimore for our second-half turnaround. The Blues went in at the break 1-0 down after the home side netted from a corner, but a brace from Malard plus a late penalty from substitute Baltimore secured a 3-1 win despite the initial setback. Our head coach explained exactly how we reversed the deficit in tricky circumstances and gave insight into what she said at half-time to galvanise the side. ‘The weather was not helpful today,’ she said. ‘Especially for a team like us who like to play on the ground, it didn't help. We probably didn't create as much as I would have liked to in the first half. ‘The second half was a better performance. We played more with the wind, which helped a little bit as well. The quality of the players who came in was good again, and they brought the impact we needed to win the game. ‘We needed to stay confident in these moments. It's really important to stay calm, even if the result is not in our hands and the weather is not helpful. I knew in the second half we had enough quality to create and to score some goals. ‘The message was around adjusting some of the defensive aspects a little but also giving the players a lot of confidence with the ball. I wanted us to keep trying, because I knew we would have opportunities, and in those moments we were clinical.’ Malard would’ve scored a hat-trick had her third goal not been ruled offside on Sunday afternoon, and it was the number nine that won the penalty on 88 minutes. Baltimore created the assist for Malard’s second and converted the spot-kick at the end of the game, leaving Bompastor full of praise for her compatriots. ‘The French players showed up today, and it was really needed,’ the head coach continued. ‘I'm happy for them, especially Sandy. She hasn't had a lot of minutes recently, but that was the best answer she could give to me. Her performance was really good. ‘When you play a team that is sitting more in the low block, she brings a lot of quality on crosses, but also on the ball, and she can beat her opponent one-on-one. That was a big help today. ‘I wasn't expecting Melvine to score from distance like that. It's a banger, as you say here! She has the ability to create those goals. She's an important player for us and I'm glad for her that she scored a really difficult goal. She could have scored an easy one just before. It makes things even better for her, and scoring like that is always good for her confidence.'

news.title: 'Wind is the worst opponent in football'
'We're in a good place'
Match report: Crystal Palace 1-3 Chelsea Women
news.body_en: A brace from Melvine Malard and a penalty scored by Sandy Baltimore ensured Chelsea recovered from a subpar first half to secure a 3-1 victory away at Crystal Palace. The sun came out on Sunday for our trip to south London after Saturday's torrential rain, but the howling wind wasn't conducive to stroking the ball around on the floor. For all of Chelsea's good work in the opening quarter-of-an-hour, it was the home side who took the lead when Molly Bartrip bundled the ball home from a corner after 20 minutes. Sonia Bompastor's team talk must've had an impact as the Blues emerged with a renewed focus after the break as Malard levelled the scores on 50 minutes with a stunning effort from the edge of the box. The match once again became tight as Palace attempted to preserve the point, but some determined work from substitute Baltimore on the left wing gave her the space to serve up an opportunity on a plate for Malard to head in her second of the afternoon. Baltimore then got herself on the scoresheet when she converted a late penalty after Malard was fouled in the box, ensuring we finished the day on a positive note after our first-half struggles. Bompastor made two alterations to her starting line-up ahead of this fixture, rotating Keira Walsh and Lauren James out of the side in place of Sjoeke Nusken and Maika Hamano. Meanwhile, Manaka Matsukubo made the squad for the first time since joining Chelsea in the summer from North Carolina Courage. The game began with the Blues pushing forward to make an immediate impact, with Alyssa Thompson causing problems for the home side down the left-hand channel and Ellie Carpenter linking up well with central striker Malard on the right. Our first real opportunity of the match came in the 14th minute, when Hamano saw her shot palmed away by the goalkeeper before Malard's shot was cleared off the line by the Palace defence. The strong winds in Sutton were always going to play a part in this contest, and made set-pieces more dangerous for both sides. When Palace swung in their second corner of the match, defender Bartrip popped up at the back post to steer the ball through the resulting melee and into the bottom corner of the net. Chelsea attempted to hit back through a Nusken power drive from inside the penalty area, but Pauline Peyraud-Magnin was able to quickly get low to snuff out the danger. Bompastor made two changes at the break, exchanging Hamano and Thompson for Erin Cuthbert and Baltimore. We showed our attacking intent when Malard went close within minutes of the restart, and it was the French international who got us back on level terms shortly afterwards. Receiving the ball 25 yards from goal from a Katie McCabe throw-in, Malard found herself in space and unleashed a stunning strike that fizzed past a helpless Peyraud-Magnin. But determined Palace were keen to fight back, and there was a let-off when former Blues striker Bethany England got herself into a good position to shoot but blazed her attempt over the bar. Our second goal of the afternoon saw Malard net her brace, but the chance was created solely by Baltimore. Driving towards the box, she sped between two Palace defenders before evading the challenge of a third and making it to the by-line to deliver a looping ball straight to the head of Malard, who wasted no time in nodding the ball home. Our noses were finally in front with 15 minutes to play, and Malard could've had her hat-trick soon afterwards but was denied by the offside flag after taking a slight touch on a brilliant ball in from McCabe. As the home side began to tire, Nusken was unlucky not to get on the scoresheet when she hit the woodwork, and with 88 minutes on the clock the French duo were decisive once again when we were awarded a penalty. Malard won the spot-kick when she was fouled inside the box, and after the number nine received some brief treatment, the ball was passed to Baltimore. The substitute stepped up and converted, securing the points after an excellent second-half display. There was to be one more positive before the final whistle, too, as Matsukubo was handed her Chelsea debut when she was introduced on 90 minutes. This was another resilient performance from the Blues, as we recorded our sixth win from seven WSL games so far this season. We go top of the WSL table, pending Manchester City's result later on. We return to Women's Champions League action when we take on Roma at Plough Lane at 5.45pm on Wednesday. news.title: Lacroix: ‘We must show the reaction of a competitor’
news.body_en: Maxence Lacroix is looking to our forthcoming games against Liverpool and Manchester United as an opportunity to put things right after our loss to Tottenham. The Blues were beaten 2-0 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, putting an abrupt end to our promising recent results. However, there is a chance to hit back in the best way possible by defeating two longstanding rivals, starting with our Carabao Cup fourth round trip to Anfield in midweek. ‘It’s a big game for us,’ said Lacroix. ‘We want to go far in this competition and it’s good that we have a game like this now. We have to move on and work on some details to be stronger in certain moments and change some situations. ‘We have to show the reaction of a competitor. We want to show another face, we want to win there, and it’s going to be a big game.’ Lacroix also offered support to Mike Penders, whose own goal gave Tottenham the lead on his first Premier League start. Xabi Alonso has confirmed the Belgian will start at Anfield on Wednesday, and Lacroix explained how the group will offer support to Penders ahead of that trip. ‘He is a young goalkeeper and he has a lot of talent,’ said Lacroix. ‘He will learn from this. This can happen in football careers and in life, everyone makes mistakes, and we have to be with him and we are going to be with him. We are behind him. He will help us this season and now we have to help him.’

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea Women line up vs Crystal Palace
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has made two changes to her Chelsea side for our Women's Super League match away at Crystal Palace. The Blues are coming off a 6-2 win over Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge last weekend and now face another test in the WSL against the newly-promoted Eagles. Bompastor has switched Keira Walsh for Sjoeke Nusken, while Maika Hamano – who scored a wonder goal against Spurs – comes in for Lauren James. Lexi Potter starts against the team where she spent two seasons on loan. She helped Palace earn promotion to the WSL in 2023/24 and returned to spend a full campaign in the top flight the following year. And after completing her recovery from injury and scoring a hat-trick for the Under-18s last weekend, summer signing Manaka Matsukubo is named on the bench for the first time this season. news.title: Caicedo: 'Everybody knows what we need to improve'
news.body_en: Moises Caicedo didn’t search for excuses in his post-match media duties after our defeat to Tottenham Hotspur. And his message was clear: ‘Everybody knows what we need to improve’. The Blues entered yesterday’s game at Stamford Bridge after back-to-back top-flight wins that had seen Bournemouth and then Everton convincingly beaten. We had also not tasted defeat on home soil this season. As Xabi Alonso accepted after the game, we were not at our best across the 90 minutes. Yet we did create chances. Cole Palmer, Jordan Henderson, Morgan Rogers and Pedro Neto all tested Antonin Kinsky in the opening period. Yet in a tight second half, Tottenham broke the deadlock by forcing an own goal from Mike Penders following a corner. Mathys Tel then netted late on to seal the win, with the Blues down to ten men after Cole Palmer was sent off. Caicedo, who wore the captain’s armband, was naturally disappointed with the result and accepted the Blues must learn from the painful defeat. He said: ‘We need to be focused during the whole game because if you switch off for one second, you get punished. ‘We need to learn from this because we need to stop this from happening and we need to maintain the clean sheet for the whole game. ‘It was a tough one, but we need to keep going because there are more games in front of us and we want to do better.’ The Ecuadorian midfielder added: ‘Everybody knows what we need to improve. We are going to think about this game because we need to be up there in the table.  We need to learn from this and for sure we are going to be up there [at the end of the season].’ For Caicedo, the game saw his third start in succession after overcoming an early-season injury. The 24-year-old was impressive in the middle of the pitch, winning a game-high four interceptions and making two tackles. ‘I tried to do my best and help the team and for sure I’m feeling better game by game,’ he explained. ‘This one was a tough game but I want to keep doing well and improving what I need to improve because I want to be someone that helps the team in every moment.’

news.title: Xabi Alonso on his confidence in Mike Penders and Liverpool decision
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has emphasised his Chelsea team ‘win and lose together’ and reaffirmed his confidence in Mike Penders, who the Blues manager confirmed will start against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup. The Belgian goalkeeper made his first Premier League start in yesterday’s game against Tottenham Hotspur and produced impressive first-half stops to deny Omar Marmoush and Mathys Tel. Unfortunately, in the second period, an own goal from Penders under pressure from Jan Paul van Hecke enabled Tottenham to take the lead. It was one of the visitors doubled late on to claim a rare win at Stamford Bridge. Alonso stressed the importance of everyone learning and improving following the defeat, including our 21-year-old goalkeeper. ‘It’s part of the business; you need to deal with mistakes and we keep confidence in Mike and he will be in goal against Liverpool,' the Blues manager said. ‘We win and we lose together and it’s part of the job to deal with mistakes, myself as well as everyone. ‘We support Mike and Geo (Quenda) as well, the guys starting their first [Premier League] games. He will want to prove he can do better - and we also have to show that.’

Premier League 2 report: Cobham Next Gen 2-2 Liverpool
news.body_en: Chelsea Cobham Next Gen were forced to settle for a point in Premier League 2 this afternoon after a 2-2 draw against Liverpool at Kingsmeadow. Harrison McMahon broke the deadlock inside two minutes with a powerful finish into the bottom corner. Sol Gordon then added to the scoreline midway through the opening period with a first-time strike beyond Harvey Davies to put the Blues in control. Minutes later, though, we were pegged back as Will Wright made it 2-1. Although we went in ahead at the break, Liverpool scored another early in the second half through a Jayden Danns free-kick. Both sides pushed for a late winner, but the spoils were shared. Chelsea set the tone immediately, scoring within two minutes through McMahon. Chizaram Ezenwata picked up the ball centrally and turned before playing a pass into McMahon’s path, and the midfielder made no mistake with his low-driven strike across goal. Ezenwata, who claimed the assist for the opener, caused the Liverpool’s backline constant problems, getting on the ball in deep areas and driving forwards. He wasn’t far away from doubling our lead when he found half a yard on Reds defender Talla Ndiaye, but his effort went just wide. Our speed constantly caused issues for the visitors' defence, with Mathis Eboue and Gordon enjoying plenty of success down the flanks. It was the latter who doubled our advantage, finishing a well-worked move. Ezenwata held the ball up well and forced his marker to bring him down. That enabled Kendry Paez to emerge with the ball and burst forward. Just as Ecuadorian looked like he was going to shoot, he instead chopped inside onto his right foot and selflessly passed to Gordon, who dispatched a fine finish past Davies. Five minutes after Gordon scored, Wright pulled one back for the visitors, capitalising on their only meaningful chance of the half. After the break, Liverpool pulled themselves back level with Danns converting from a free-kick. He placed his strike into the bottom corner, beyond the outstretched glove of Freddy Bernal. Liverpool continued to put us under pressure, with Prince Cisse hitting the post and Oliver O'Connor missing a clear-cut chance. We pushed for a late winner but were ultimately forced to settle for a point. After six games, this draw leaves us on 13 points in Premier League 2 and in second position. The league leaders are ahead via goal difference with a game in hand. Cobham Next Gen are kickstart their UEFA Youth League campaign on Wednesday 28 October, when we face Estonian side Flora Tallinn at the Lillekula Stadium. The game gets underway at 5pm BST and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: Xabi Alonso on Tottenham defeat: 'We all take the blame'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso was disappointed with the performance and result against Tottenham Hotspur and accepted his Chelsea side 'can do better' after succumbing to a two-goal defeat at Stamford Bridge. During a rain-soaked 90 minutes in SW6, both sides created goalscoring opportunities across the 90 minutes. Cole Palmer forced Antonin Kinsky into a good first-half save, and Jordan Henderson, Morgan Rogers and Pedro Neto were also denied by the Tottenham goalkeeper. Mike Penders made good stops of his own, first to deny Omar Marmoush and then Mathys Tel. However, with 13 minutes remaining, Tottenham forced a Penders own goal from a corner and, after Palmer was dismissed for two yellow cards, Tel struck late on to seal a rare Spurs' victory at Stamford Bridge. Alonso was honest in his post-match assessment, acknowledging the performance was not at the level the Blues had displayed in our back-to-back wins over Bournemouth and Everton. ‘We all take the blame for the result and for the performance,' he said. 'Today we were not at our best. I felt that in the second half, the game was even and could have gone either way. Once we conceded that first goal, and then with the red card, it was difficult.' The Blues manager continued: 'In the second half, it was tight, with some half-chances for them and half-chances for us. It was about taking a moment and once we conceded the first goal, it conceded everything. Then, when we wanted to have a reaction, we got the red card. Then it went the other way. 'We can do better. It's one to reflect after this big game that it was against a good opponent. And the performance, it's one to improve.' The Blues' preparation for the game was disrupted with Joao Pedro sustaining an injury in training on the eve of Tottenham's visit. And Alonso said the absence of the Brazilian forward did mean a late change to the game plan was needed. He said: 'We had to take many decisions in a short time. What we had been working on in the week, you need to be flexible and adapt. So it changed the idea we had a little bit, but this is football, and it can happen. 'It’s no secret that with Joao we are better, but it’s not about talking about the players missing. It’s about the players who were on the pitch. We can do better and we have to be critical of ourselves.'

news.title: Highlights: Chelsea 0-2 Spurs
Match report: Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham Hotspur
news.body_en: It proved a disappointing evening for the Blues at Stamford Bridge as we were beaten by Tottenham Hotspur. For much of the contest, little separated the two sides. In the opening period, Cole Palmer and Jordan Henderson forced Antonin Kinsky into good saves. Mike Penders, meanwhile, produced good stops to deny Omar Marmoush and Mathys Tel. The second period remained tight, but with 13 minutes to play, a Tottenham corner ended up in the Blues' goal via the hand of Penders, who was put under pressure by Jan Paul van Hecke. Palmer was then shown a red card after receiving two yellows inside ten minutes, and Tel netted late on for Tottenham to condemn the Blues to defeat. Xabi Alonso was forced to make two changes to his starting XI. Emi Martinez and Joao Pedro both missed out due to injuries –the latter sustaining an issue in training yesterday – and were replaced by Penders and Geovany Quenda. The opening 45 minutes were played in a downpour. It meant every touch had to be precise and every pass weighted perfectly. The Blues looked more threatening in the early stages and kept Tottenham at arm's length. Our first chance of note was fashioned as the game approached the quarter-hour mark. Pedro Neto started it as he won the ball near the corner flag and fed it to Morgan Rogers inside the box. The England international laid it first-time to Palmer, who whipped his shot to the far post from an acute angle. However, Antonin Kinsky saved well. As the half progressed, Spurs took a stranglehold of possession. Mohammed Kudus had the visitors' first shot of the evening – an attempt from inside the box that flew wide – before a good chance was created for Omar Marmoush from 10 yards. Penders reacted quickly to produce an excellent stop. The Belgian goalkeeper produced an even better save soon after, rushing out and diving at the feet of Mathys Tel to deny the forward's left-footed strike. Alonso's side responded to the Spurs' attempts. The first came following a mistake from Kinsky, which enabled Neto, Rogers and Palmer to exchange one-touch passes in the Tottenham penalty area and lay the ball to Henderson. The Blues midfielder attempted to guide his finish into the corner, but put it close enough to Kinsky to allow the goalkeeper to save. Rogers was next denied as he drove a left-footed strike at goal, but the offside flag was subsequently raised. Our final chance of the half fell to Neto, with a free-kick worked short to the Portuguese winger. He drove his shot to the near post, yet Kinsky got down to save and the game was goalless at the interval. The Blues have often made fast starts to second halves this season, but both sides nullified each other's threat in 15 minutes after the break. Much of the game was played in midfield, with attacks breaking down or being snuffed out. It wasn't until the hour mark that a shot was registered that threatened to break the deadlock. It came from Neto, who, after winning the ball and finding Palmer, reacted quickest to a rebound inside the area and drove a shot at Kinsky. The Tottenham stopper beat it behind for a corner. Our first change of the afternoon came soon after, with Marco Palestra coming on for Hato. The Italian dropped into a role on the left of our defence. Estevao's introduction followed; he replaced Quenda. Before the Brazilian's introduction came the game's biggest flashpoint. After Caicedo launched a counter-attack and was fouled in the process by van de Ven, a run from Palmer was halted by Mateus Fernandes falling and grabbing the ball. Several players came together, and three yellow cards followed, one of which went to Palmer. From the restart, we fashioned an opportunity as Palmer and Henderson combined to get Estevao in on goal from a tight angle. He fired at goal but into the side netting. With 13 minutes to play, and somewhat against the run of play, Tottenham went ahead. A corner was delivered into the Chelsea penalty area and van Hecke put Penders under pressure. The ball struck the hand of the Blues goalkeeper and deflected into our net despite Maxence Lacroix's efforts. Our task got harder as, three minutes later, Palmer caught Conor Gallagher in midfield and referee Chris Kavanagh deemed it worthy of a second yellow card, and a red followed. The game was effectively killed late on as a run and finish from Tel gave Tottenham a two-goal advantage in the closing stages, which they were able to see out to claim victory. The Blues are back in action on Wednesday evening as we take on Liverpool in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup. news.title: Cesar Azpilicueta joins Chelsea Legends squad taking on Tottenham
news.body_en: On the day the current Chelsea team play Spurs, another of our Champions League-winning captains is confirmed for when Stamford Bridge hosts a clash between old rivals on Saturday 27 March. The Chelsea Legends versus Tottenham Legends match will take place on Easter Weekend and raise crucial funds for Chelsea Foundation and its work bringing people together, creating healthier lives and shaping brighter futures in our local communities. Cesar Azpilicueta, the sixth-highest appearance-maker in our history who won every major trophy available to him while at Chelsea, joins another successful skipper, John Terry, plus Eden Hazard, Oscar and Chelsea Women's legendary captain Katie Chapman as the players announced so far. They will be stirring great memories when they return to Stamford Bridge next spring with more legends to be announced in the coming weeks. news.title: Alonso explains Joao Pedro absence against Tottenham
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has explained why Joao Pedro is not in the Chelsea squad for this afternoon’s game against Tottenham Hotspur – and emphasised the qualities Mike Penders and Geovany Quenda will bring on their full Premier League debuts. We are back at Stamford Bridge this afternoon for what the Blues manager expects to be an ‘intense game’ against our London rivals, whom we are aiming to defeat for an unprecedented seventh success in the Premier League. Alonso has made two changes to the team that started our win at Everton last weekend. One was expected as Penders replaces the injured Emi Martinez, who underwent jaw surgery after a nasty collision with Jarrad Branthwaite at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. The other is the absence of Joao Pedro, with Alonso explaining the Brazilian was ruled out of the contest yesterday. ‘He felt something yesterday in training,’ Alonso said. ‘At the moment, he has some fluid [around the injury], so we have to do some tests to see how big is the injury is. For sure, it’s a disappointment, but we need to carry on.’ Quenda is the man Alonso has opted to replace Joao Pedro with in the starting XI. It is the Portuguese winger’s first top-flight start in English football after his arrival in the summer. He has many qualities,’ Alonso said when asked about Quenda’s selection.’ He attacks the space well, is good with the ball, and is a threat. He’s been training well, and all the players will have their opportunities. Sometimes, they have to be more patient. Geo has been patient, and today it’s a big game to make his debut as a starter. 'We want to have mobility and to be fluid, so that we are not static and for sure with Geo we have those qualities.' Penders, meanwhile, starts in the Premier League for the first time, having made his debut off the bench against Everton last weekend. ‘I believe in every player we have and today it’s the first start in the PL for Mike,’ explained Alonso. ‘He showed last weekend against Everton that the can have a good impact. We need to deal with injuries and now he has a good chance, and we are fully confident.’ A big-game atmosphere is building at Stamford Bridge ahead of kick-off, and Alonso has highlighted the important role the Blues supporters play across the 90 minutes. 'It will be an intense game at a high tempo and high intensity on the pitch and in the stands. A proper derby. We expect an intense game with different moments for everything, with our qualities and the qualities of Tottenham. So it’s going to be very interesting.'

news.title: Under-18 Premier League report: Chelsea 4-1 Ipswich Town
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s came from behind to secure an impressive 4-1 victory over Ipswich Town at Cobham in the Under-18 Premier League, with Jacob Dako scoring a brace and Jacob Hall and Heze Grimwade always in target. After dominating the opening exchanges, the Blues fell behind in the 17th minute as Joel Ladegbaye swept home following an Ipswich counter-attack. We reacted positively, pushing for the leveller and probing the Ipswich back line on various occasions. Unfortunately, we couldn't apply a finishing touch before the break and went into the half-time interval a goal behind. The Blues continued to push in the second period, and our efforts paid off in the 66th minute as Dako found the net. That broke Ipswich's resistance and Hall netted soon after to put us ahead. We held that advantage until the closing stages – and then extended it as Ipswich attempted to salvage a point. Dako completed his double before Grimwade netted an excellent free-kick in stoppage time to seal a 4-1 victory. The Blues controlled the opening 15 minutes, although we were unable to consistently threaten the visitors' goal. Jashayde Greenwood did force a save from Ipswich goalkeeper Edward Twyman and Dako fired over the crossbar. After 17 minutes, we were punished on the counter, with Callum Stewart playing the final pass across the face of goal to enable Ladegbaye to sweep home and make it 1-0. We had a chance to level almost immediately, as Twyman raced out to clear his lines and missed the ball. Grimwade chased and lunged towards the ball, aiming to poke it into an empty net, but Pedro Felicio was there first to spare the goalkeeper’s blushes. We continued to search for an equaliser throughout the rest of the half. Ibrahim Rabbaj came close as he drifted inside and received the ball, but his left-footed attempt went just wide of the far post. We remained a persistent threat down the right, and Isaac McGillvary played a give-and-go with Rabbaj before cutting a pass to Greenwood. The Blues striker’s first-time shot was just off target. Towards the end of the half, Isaac Badu fashioned a great opportunity to level. The Portuguese youth international wriggled through midfield and played the ball to Greenwood, who lined up the shot before opting to tee up Rabbaj instead. But his shot was blocked and remained a goal down at the break. After the interval, it was more of the same, with the Blues holding onto the ball for long spells. Dako had two good chances in quick succession but was unable to convert either. Substitute Gabriel Sambou created the first, as he crossed into the penalty area for Dako, but he didn’t get enough on his header to steer it goalwards. Moments later, Greenwood drove towards goal and shimmied inside before laying the ball off to the midfielder, whose shot was dragged just wide. He was eventually rewarded with a goal, though. Captain Dante Waite played the ball behind the Tractor Boys’ defence, and Dako was able to tuck his finish into the net for his fifth league goal of the campaign. The Blues were a lot more like ourselves after Dako’s goal and, after Sambou had came agonisingly with a shot cleared off the line by Felicio. we scored our second just four minutes later. Hall gave us the advantage as he quickest when Twyman spilled a Dako free kick to place the ball into the corner. Having taken the lead, the Blues were oozing with confidence in the latter stages, and we began getting far more shots on target. Ipswich showed more attacking intent once they had fallen behind, but our defence handled the onslaught superbly. Dako then completed his brace to make it 3-1 with a neat finish into the bottom corner. The visitors' best chance fell to Kyle Messenger, who seemed set to halve the deficit. Toby Bell’s initial save was very impressive but the ball fell into Messenger’s path; fortunately, Hall made a fantastic recovery run and block. Grimwade got in on the action with the final kick of the game, scoring from a set piece once again. The 16-year-old wrapped the free-kick into the top left corner to end the game in style. This victory means we remain top of the table on 21 points, having won seven matches and scoring 37 goals. The Blues also extended our perfect run to five games. Chelsea Under-18s are back on the road next week when we face West Ham United on Saturday 31 October. The game gets underway at 11am BST and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: From Where I Sit: The Harding family 💙
Alonso on harnessing passion and energy of ‘electric’ derby atmosphere
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso expects Chelsea supporters to create an 'electric' atmosphere inside Stamford Bridge during today's game against Tottenham Hotspur, which he believes will show the Premier League at its very best. Few occasions get Stamford Bridge bouncing quite like the visit of London rivals Tottenham to SW6; it's one of the first fixtures Blues supporters look out for when the Premier League fixtures are released each season. This match will be no different, with Alonso's side going into tomorrow's game in good form after back-to-back wins over Bournemouth and Everton. We are also looking for a club-record seventh consecutive home league victory over Spurs. Alonso is set to experience the atmosphere of a Chelsea versus Tottenham derby for the first time as Blues manager. But he knows what to expect and hopes the energy provided by the crowd can help his players to victory. ‘We are expecting a good atmosphere,’ he said. ‘Electric, with good energy, knowing that in a derby this passion is really in the air in the stadium. ‘We need to use it in a proper way because this is all about those games when you feel that excitement is something that you need. You don't need extra motivation; that will come naturally because of the history of the derby and because this is a top game. ‘We need that connection with the crowd in good moments. There will be tough moments, but we need to pull together and play our game. For me, it's fundamental that we play our game on the pitch. ‘The players, they do their best, but when the crowd is playing the game, is living it, that's the good thing about the Premier League. I think the crowd plays the game as well. It's not that they just watch the game. ‘They have great influence. When I say that spontaneously some energy is created in this league, it's because they feel that moment that: “Yes, I like what I see” and it's a big boost for the team.’ However, the Chelsea manager is aware that such emotionally charged atmospheres also require the players on the pitch to keep a level head to balance the passion with maturity, admitting that managing such situations in the Premier League is always a challenge mentally, but especially on occasions such as this. ‘It is very difficult,’ added Alonso. ‘That's why I've mentioned a few times that to find total dominance, a game when you are in full control and that you have no problems like in other leagues, it's difficult to find that in the Premier League unless you have become a top, top team. ‘That's why you can't rest when you are 2-0 up, because you know that if you concede one, the energy is coming, and you need to control that momentum. You can have mental preparation, but you need composure to deal with those moments. ‘I think that even in the Everton first half, we were 0-0, but there were a few [challenging] moments – 10 minutes of corner, throw-in, corner, throw-in. To go through those moments and to say, “Be calm guys, we know what we have to do, we have prepared for this and the other momentum will come”, for me it's fundamental.’ Don't miss your chance to experience the London derby in VIP style. news.title: Chelsea vs Tottenham: All you need to know
news.body_en: High-flying Chelsea return to the house of fun for a 5.30pm Saturday kick-off against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League at Stamford Bridge. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to derby day in west London. Over the coming weekends Chelsea host successive league games against traditional foes before the next international break and they do not come weightier than this cross-city clash of west and north. It is the Blues’ first game this season in a time-slot that has not recently been fruitful, with just seven points taken from the last possible 21 and a current run of two straight losses. However, we are undefeated in the past eight London derbies home and away played at this time, including a 1-0 defeat of our capital rivals in the reverse fixture last season. Roberto De Zerbi’s visitors were winless in all top-flight games this season until beating Frank Lampard’s Coventry City 3-1 at home on Monday, climbing out of the relegation zone as a result. Xabi Alonso’s Blues made what felt like a step forward with Saturday’s 2-0 victory at bogey side Everton and returned to the UEFA Champions League qualification places. Chelsea have taken the lead in six of our seven league outings to date – the complete opposite to Spurs – and have taken an average of just four minutes to open the scoring at the Bridge. Last May, the corresponding fixture ended 2-1 with Enzo Fernandez and Andrey Santos netting for the hosts to extend Spurs’ relegation reckoning to the final day. Chelsea have a remarkable home record against our second-oldest top-flight capital rivals and can make club history by beating the Cockerels an unprecedented seventh time in a row in the Premier League. Up to now, the Blues have beaten the Lilywhites 83 times across all competitions, more than any other opponent. Alonso confirmed in his pre-match press conference after Friday's training session that Malo Gusto was fit to return against Tottenham, having missed our win at Everton the previous weekend, but Pep Chavarria, Jamie Gittens and Emiliano Martinez remain unavailable. 'Malo is fine,' the Blues manager explained. 'Pep is training a little bit more, but he is not going to make it [for the Tottenham game]. 'Emi had the surgery and day-by-day he is feeling better, but we still need to wait. A few weeks. Hopefully, less than more, but we need to wait.' Emmanuel Emegha will also miss out. The striker has yet to feature since arriving this summer, but is making progress in his comeback. ‘He’s feeling better, but we need to wait,' said Alonso. Chelsea are undefeated in eight league derbies with this kick-off time, since Boxing Day 2020, winning seven, including at Tottenham a year ago at the Bridge through Joao Pedro’s stealthy finish. Down the Thames at Craven Cottage in mid-January 2021, Mason Mount settled the result late on, and some time after Antonee Robinson had been red carded. Four months later in the return against Fulham at the Bridge, Kai Havertz struck twice without reply to claim all the points in the west London derby. The German also drew early first blood at Crystal Palace in April, with Christian Pulisic quickly making it two inside 10 minutes. Kurt Zouma added a third for the visitors before Christian Benteke pulled one back for the shell-shocked hosts. Pulisic’s second made the last quarter-hour comfortable and it finished 4-1 to Chelsea. Two weeks later, at West Ham United’s London Stadium, Timo Werner netted the only goal of the game in the first half, Fabian Balbuema’s 81st-minute dismissal easing any nerves. At Brentford in October 2021, with fans back in the stadium, Ben Chilwell was the only name on the scoresheet, on the brink of half-time, with our only shot on target as Edouard Mendy kept the Bees at bay for Thomas Tuchel. A year ago at the Bridge, against this weekend’s visitors, with early fireworks fizzing the night sky, Moises Caicedo pounced on defensive uncertainty to set up Joao Pedro for the 1-0 winner. At the end of January 2026, Jarrod Bowen curled in West Ham’s opener in west London and Crysencio Summerville doubled their shock lead before the break. But Nuno Espírito Santo’s side were taken to task in the second half, with Joao Pedro’s close-range header halving the deficit before Marc Cucurella’s brave dive produced the leveller. Joao Pedro turned provider for Fernandez to drive in what proved the decisive finish, after which Anthony Taylor resolved a stoppage-time fracas with a red card for visiting defender Jean-Clair Todibo. Tottenham are Morgan Rogers’ favourite opponent, the Chelsea forward scoring a career-high four times against the Lilywhites. The Blues have won 55.7 per cent of ground duels – the most in this season’s top flight. Chelsea have now scored three goals in the opening minute of a half in the Premier League to date, our joint-most in a single campaign (alongside the entire 2011/12 season). Until last Saturday at Everton, Chelsea had not kept a clean sheet in the Premier League since the same 2-0 scoreline at home to Brentford on 17 January, 22 games ago. Pedro Neto had never previously scored twice in a Premier League game, though he had netted a hat-trick for the Blues against Hull City in the FA Cup. news.title: Lacroix shares his journey from village life to the bright lights of the Bridge
news.body_en: Maxence Lacroix discusses his untypical footballing origins, in a farming village in the Dordogne region, and reveals his cultural hinterland in a wide-ranging interview for the matchday programme for Saturday’s Premier League game against Tottenham Hotspur. The France international defender grew up as one of a handful of kids playing football in the surrounding villages, where his parents both worked in the medical profession, and has risen to become a serial winner. 'It’s a farming village and there were maybe 300 people, with maybe five young children, because there were a lot of older people, or people who worked on the farms. My mother is a doctor, a general practitioner. And my father, he is working as a resuscitation nurse in the hospital. 'When I was young, I was quite close to wanting to be a vet, because animals were always close to me, you know. 'I started playing football at four. I was a goalkeeper, because my father was a goalkeeper. He put me on the field, because he loved football – he still does – and he said to me: "Okay, now it’s the time for you to start playing too".' The rest, as they say, is history, and now the 26-year-old is enjoying a year to remember, having gone to the FIFA World Cup off the back of a UEFA Conference League triumph with his former club Crystal Palace, then returned to London to begin the next chapter of his career with Chelsea. 'It’s going good,' he says of the season so far. 'I think we are in a better way, and you know, it was really quick for me, because I just left the national team, I had just a little bit of holidays and then I came back directly to playing the first game. So no, it was strange, but now I feel really settled in the team, so this is really good for me. 'It is fun, and it is a big team, you know – the players here are the best in the league. So I’m really happy to represent the badge and to be part of this big journey.' Elsewhere in the programme, club historian Rick Glanvill reflects on the impact Matthew Harding made on the club, as we mark the 30th anniversary of his tragic death in a helicopter crash on the way back from an away game at Bolton Wanderers in October 1996. The team that Harding’s investment helped to build went on to become one of the most cherished in Chelsea history, and their 6-1 win at White Hart Lane in December 1997 is the focus of our Greatest Games feature. Then there is all the info you need on the game ahead, plus the latest from around the club, including columns from Xabi Alonso and Reece James. So be sure to pick up your copy from the programme sellers around Stamford Bridge or order online from our publications partner, Reach Sport.

The Metropolitan Police Service (MPS) has informed the club that on Saturday, Live Facial Recognition (LFR) will be deployed during the policing operation for the Chelsea versus Tottenham fixture.  The deployment follows the established stakeholder engagement approach previously used for football-related LFR deployments.  The two locations will be Earl's Court and West Brompton and two LFR vans will be deployed across these locations before the game. Signage will be deployed outside the zone of recognition in line with MPS LFR policy. The watchlist will contain individuals subject to Football Banning Orders relating to either club, together with persons wanted or missing for serious offences and those sought on warrants issued by HMCTS. There are measures in place and strong sanctions against offenders to tackle discriminatory, anti-social and criminal behaviour. This could include suspension from attending all Chelsea matches, as well as potential police action. If you witness any anti-social or discriminatory behaviour on matchday, please report it to us.  Click below to use our reporting form for home matchdays.  This link will be active and the form available for use from three hours prior to kick-off until one hour after the final whistle.  - Click to access the reporting form At other times, click here to make a report. You can also report it in real time by using our reporting number. All Premier League matches from 17 to 25 October are dedicated to No Room For Racism, reinforcing a collective commitment to tackling all forms of discrimination and promoting diversity within football. With Saturday being our home match during this period, a film will be shown inside Stamford Bridge, celebrating diversity as one of the game's greatest strengths. It will also highlight the impact racism can have on players, their families and communities, and encourages fans to challenge and report discriminatory behaviour. The No Room For Racism message will be displayed throughout the stadium, and players will be taking the knee to show solidarity against discrimination and send a clear message that racism has no place in our game or wider society. Supporters are reminded that engineering work affecting the District Line, with Fulham Broadway Station closed on Saturday, may have an impact on journeys to and from the match. Chelsea Football Club announces multi-year sleeve partnership with Sokin
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club can today announce a multi-year partnership with Sokin, the embedded finance and payments company used by businesses worldwide. Sokin will be named a Principal Partner and Official Business Payments and FX Partner of Chelsea FC and Chelsea FC Women. As a Principal Partner, Sokin will be represented on the sleeves of the Chelsea FC men’s, women’s and academy home, away, and third kits from the 2026/27 season. The partnership brings together two ambitious London-headquartered organisations with worldwide reach – a club with millions of fans across the world and a fintech platform through which businesses move more than $11 billion a year. A club of Chelsea’s scale works in many currencies every day, with partners, competitions and supporters around the world, and needs a financial partner built to handle that. Sokin gives finance teams business payments, multi-currency accounts, foreign exchange, checkout and treasury in one place, so they spend less time juggling banks and providers and keep more of what they move. As Official Business Payments and FX Partner, Sokin will simplify how Chelsea FC sends, receives and manages money in the currencies the club operates in. The Sokin logo will feature on the sleeve of the Chelsea shirt for the first time when the men’s team host Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday 24 October. Jason Gannon, President at Chelsea FC, said: 'At Chelsea, we seek to partner with organisations that share our ambition and innovative mindset. Sokin’s expertise in business payments, and their focus on making both simpler for the businesses they serve, makes them a natural fit for the Club. We are pleased to welcome Sokin to the Chelsea family and look forward to working together in the years ahead.' Vroon Modgill, CEO and founder at Sokin, said: 'Chelsea plays on the biggest stage in world football, and its business runs in dozens of currencies. Sokin was built for that with regulated, multi-currency payments and foreign exchange for organisations that operate internationally. 'We’re proud to be the platform behind the business payments and FX of one of the most iconic teams in football. Sokin’s platform serves businesses in more than 170 countries. We’re thrilled to be partners for the season ahead. An organisation as sophisticated as Chelsea doesn’t leave its finances to chance.'

news.title: Look who’s joined us on the sleeve 👀🔵
Alonso targeting a ‘complete’ performance to continue good run
news.body_en: Tottenham Hotspur's visit to Stamford Bridge tomorrow is the first of three high-profile fixtures in the space of the week for Xabi Alonso's side – and the Blues manager has stressed the qualities that must be shown to start with a positive result. We have lost to the side from north London just once in our past 41 meetings in SW6, but Alonso knows that record counts for nothing come kick-off on Saturday, when a new chapter in the rivalry will be written. With the Blues targeting a third straight league success for the first time since the start of this year, and Tottenham hoping to pick up a second victory this week, there is plenty on the line. Alonso knows what to expect. ‘We need to have a very complete game,’ he said. ‘Offensively, defensively, mentality-wise going through difficult moments, as there will be moments for everything. ‘We need to prove again we can continue our run, knowing it’s a special game. We need to play with our head, heart, with intelligence but with passionate energy. We will need many things tomorrow.’ On Tottenham, Alonso added: ‘I’ve seen a good team even in bad results, so we’re expecting a tough game against good opposition who do many good things. 'We need to be prepared for what to do in different moments with the ball. It’s going to be game eight [in the Premier League this season], so it’s still early days for everything.’ The meeting with Tottenham is the first of three high-profile fixtures in quick succession. Next week we travel to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup fourth round before hosting Manchester United. Alonso is excited for what is to come, and wants to see his side rise to the challenge and prove their credentials. ‘It was a matter of time until we had big games and this week we have three massive games against top clubs. This happens in the Premier League; this is not news. So we take it step by step, and we start tomorrow.’ Don't miss your chance to experience the London derby in VIP style. news.title: Ticketing update
news.body_en: As part of our commitment to provide transparency for our supporters across our ticketing policies and procedures, Chelsea FC is pleased to share an update on the progress of the newly introduced systems so far this season. The ticket application window was introduced for men's team matches for the 2026/27 season following supporter feedback regarding the ticketing process. After extensive fan consultation with multiple fan groups, the Fan Advisory Board and a supporter town hall, the ticket application window has been established to streamline the ticket purchase journey, make it fairer and more accessible for genuine Chelsea fans to purchase tickets, and reduce the risk of bot and tout activity. Similar systems are operated by a number of other Premier League clubs. We are pleased to share the results of the first six ticket application windows this season, to update supporters on how the process is working. Based on the data available for the ticket application windows this season, an eligible member applying for an individual match ticket via the ticket application window stood a 68% chance of securing a ticket. Overall, 99% of eligible members who applied for every Premier League game, have successfully secured at least one ticket, via the ticket application window, the ticket exchange or ticket forwarding, demonstrating the system provides greater opportunity for a larger number of fans to attend matches at Stamford Bridge. So far this season, of all fans who have applied in at least one ticket application window, 80% have secured a ticket for at least one match. The most in-demand fixtures are sold using a loyalty point threshold, to prioritise loyalty and regular match-going supporters. For the Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur fixtures, 46% of tickets were allocated to those who fell within the top 10% of total accumulated loyalty points. The ticket exchange and ticket forwarding function provides an additional route for supporters to access tickets. For those who were unsuccessful in the ticket application window, the ticket exchange represents a second chance of securing a ticket, with unsuccessful applicants having a minimum 48-hour priority window. We want to ensure genuine Chelsea fans are able to access tickets and we encourage all our supporters to use the ticket exchange and ticket forwarding to do so. For more information on using these mechanisms,  you can view our How-to Guides by clicking here. We also want to ensure that the next generation of Chelsea supporters have more opportunity to come to Stamford Bridge. So far this season, 76% of Junior Blue members who have applied in the ticket application window have been successful in securing at least one match ticket. The club continues to clamp down on ticket touting. In previous seasons, we have seen up to 80,000 bots per game attempt to access tickets online. Now, with the introduction of the ticket application window those using automated purchasing software are prevented from accessing on-sale windows and it enables increased monitoring of accounts to identify suspicious activity. We also continue to operate ticket collection points at home and away fixtures. So far this season, we have seen a 93% non-collection rate, demonstrating that our ongoing work to identify suspicious or fraudulent accounts is working. Using this data and supporter feedback, the club will continue to review our ticketing policies and processes, sharing regular insights with the Fan Advisory Board and updating Fans’ Forums.

Cobham Unseen: pre-Tottenham (h) 💪
Xabi Alonso says Mike Penders is ready to show his qualities
news.body_en: Mike Penders is expected to start his first Premier League game when Chelsea meet Tottenham tomorrow, and Xabi Alonso is confident the 21-year-old is prepared for the challenge that awaits. Penders was introduced midway through the second half of our victory at Everton last weekend, becoming our youngest Premier League goalkeeper. He replaced Emi Martinez, who took a heavy blow to the face and has subsequently undergone surgery on his jaw. With Martinez out for what Alonso says will be a ‘few weeks’, Penders is set to don the gloves for the Blues, with a mouthwatering London derby up first. ‘He is ready,’ said Alonso in his pre-match press conference. ‘He has been training well and played a couple of cup games where he showed he has a good level. Even the other day when he came on against Everton, he showed in a few minutes his personality and qualities. ‘This is why we have a squad, to be ready for these kinds of situations, and we are fully convinced that Mike can play very well. He is a goalkeeper for now and for the future. We are looking to the next games and are happy with Mike. He is prepared.’ Penders’ assimilation into English football has been aided in the past couple of months by Martinez, who brings a vast wealth of knowledge and know-how with him. Alonso explained how the Argentinean has helped Penders, who spent last season on loan at Strasbourg having signed for Chelsea in the summer of 2024. ‘He has the support and is learning from an experienced goalkeeper in Emi, who is having a great impact on the team and on Mike. ‘That happens in a very natural way. It’s not that we say, “Dibu, you have to be a mentor and you have this certificate.” It happens naturally, spontaneously every day because Emi likes to talk, not just with the other goalkeepers, but defenders as well. ‘He is very communicative and he likes to have this sense that they are close. So it’s happening.’ 'It has been noted that Penders bears similarities to former Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who Alonso worked with at Real Madrid. Our manager agrees there are resemblances between the two beyond simply their appearance and nationality. ‘The stature, both left-footed, both dominant in the air,’ Alonso pointed out. ‘I spoke with Thibaut when he was at the World Cup and asked about Mike, and he said himself that he could see the resemblance with Mike. 'We need to help him, support him, but for sure he is a goalkeeper for the present and the future.’ Don't miss your chance to experience the London derby in VIP style. news.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Tottenham
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso confirmed Blues defender Malo Gusto is in contention to face Tottenham Hotspur tomorrow and provided updates on the fitness of Pep Chavarria, Emmanuel Emegha and Emi Martinez. The Blues welcome an old foe to Stamford Bridge tomorrow afternoon as Roberto De Zerbi brings his Spurs side to west London. We enter the game after impressive back-to-back top-flight victories: the first a 5-1 win over Bournemouth and the second a 2-0 triumph at Everton. Tottenham, meanwhile, recorded their first Premier League win of the campaign last time out. However, they are winless on the road this season. Alonso, who undertook his pre-match press conference duties after today's training session at Cobham, confirmed that Gusto was fit to return after missing our win on Merseyside last weekend. Chavarria, though, will remain absent. 'Malo is fine,' the Blues manager explained. 'Pep is training a little bit more, but he is not going to make it [for the Tottenham game]. Emegha will also miss out. The striker has yet to feature since arriving this summer, but is making progress in his comeback. ‘He’s feeling better, but we need to wait,' said Alonso. There will be no Martinez against Tottenham – or for a few weeks – due to the injury the Argentine sustained against Everton in a collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. Martinez was stretchered off in the second half and was taken to hospital for further checks, after which he underwent surgery on his jaw. Alonso confirmed the goalkeeper is doing well, but he will be sidelined for the matches ahead. 'Emi is doing better,' he said. 'He had the surgery and day by day he is feeling better, but we still need to wait. A few weeks. Hopefully, less than more, but we need to wait. 'The good thing is that he is feeling better and we need to listen to his feelings, the opinions of the doctors, the specialists, the surgeons. Considering it was a bad one, he is doing good.' news.title: Alonso Press Conference 🎙️
Lexi Potter on learnings from Keira Walsh and facing her former side
news.body_en: If there ever was an ideal role model for a young midfielder in the women’s game, it would be serial winner Keira Walsh. Our Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter is now learning alongside her in the Blues first team, and she is thriving. It’s more than just master and apprentice, though. Potter’s calm head and confidence on the ball in the holding role has allowed Walsh to play higher up the pitch, to great success. When we sat down with the 20-year-old prodigy, she gave some insight into how the pair work together, and also into the general mood inside the camp at Chelsea. ‘Keira gives me a lot of confidence when I’m playing alongside her,’ Potter told us. ‘Especially when I'm receiving the ball out of possession. She gives me a lot of good information. We see the game in a similar way, and we're on the same page a lot of the time when we’re trying to progress the ball forward from a central area. ‘We’re in a really nice place as a team. For a while now, it's been really positive, and I think you can see it in the performances that everyone's working and fighting for each other.’ This Sunday, we face newly-promoted Crystal Palace away from home. Potter is best qualified to talk about the Eagles, having helped them earn promotion to the Women’s Super League in 2023/24. She immediately returned for a second season-long loan, gaining valuable experience in the WSL. Now, they are back in the top flight and the midfielder passes along some insight on what to expect from them. ‘I think it'll be a good game,’ she says. 'Having been at the club for two seasons, I know a few of the girls, and I’m looking forward to the game. ‘It was really special to be involved in their promotion. It was my first year in senior football, and I really enjoyed that season. I had a lot of opportunities, which I was grateful for. It was a really good season, and I  enjoyed it. ‘I was only 17, so I wasn't allowed to go for the full celebrations. But yeah, they were good; they were fun. It was a nice end to a good season. ‘The second season was a slightly different season to the first one. It was obviously a lot harder teams that we played. In terms of competition for places, it was a lot harder, and it was a different mindset. Potter added: ‘Getting minutes in the WSL at Palace really helped me because playing time is so valuable when you are developing. That exposure to the WSL really helped me during the loan. ‘When you’re a newly-promoted side, playing against the big teams was a really big challenge, and that’s always good for long-term development. I'm still in touch with a couple of the girls. I know Aimee (Everett), the captain, quite well and I speak to her fairly regularly. She really looked after me when I was there. ‘A few of the staff members there were really like impactful and really beneficial for me and my journey. I'm very lucky to have crossed paths with a lot of good people at the club. ‘They've had a good start to the season. They've picked up some really good results, so they'll put up a good challenge. They'll defend well, and we need to be on our game and try and break them down.’ Having now cemented her place in the Blues first team, our discussion concluded with our question about what she would say to any young players in the Chelsea Academy who are hoping to follow in her footsteps. ‘I'd say work hard and be patient,’ she concluded. ‘Your time will come. You just have to stay ready and work hard for it.’

news.title: Freddy Bernal signs new deal
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club is pleased to announce that Cobham Next Gen goalkeeper Freddy Bernal has signed a new contract, keeping him at the club until at least June 2029. Having joined Chelsea’s Academy as an Under-8, Bernal became a full-time scholar in 2025/26 and established himself for the Under-18s, winning the Under-18s Premier League title at Stamford Bridge. Bernal has since become a consistent presence between the sticks for Cobham Next Gen, making eight appearances so far and keeping a clean sheet in our latest EFL Trophy clash against Reading. The 18-year-old also gained valuable European experience last season in the UEFA Youth League, producing some standout performances against Bayern Munich, Benfica and Ajax. A reliable presence in goal, Bernal has demonstrated maturity throughout his progression at Chelsea. His form has also been recognised internationally with regular invitations to England youth camps. Having previously represented the Young Lions at Under-17 and Under-18 level, he featured for the Under-19s during the September and October international window.

news.title: FPL 2026/27: Chelsea Gameweek eight
news.body_en: Chelsea have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues. Here, we look at which Blues players are the best value-for-money picks, why Morgan Rogers (£8.0m) is Chelsea’s most popular player this week and who you should captain in Gameweek 8. The deadline is 6.30pm BST on Friday ahead of Nottingham Forest’s trip to Ipswich Town. Morgan Rogers (£8.0m) is the most popular Chelsea player ahead of Gameweek 8 with over 170,000 transfers in. The Englishman has risen in price to £8.0m after starting the season at £7.5m and is the most-selected midfielder in Fantasy, with an ownership of over 48%. No Chelsea player has registered more expected goal involvement (xGI) than Rogers’ tally of 3.43; on top of that, he has notched 19 shots and created an impressive 13 chances. In an Aston Villa shirt, Rogers picked up three attacking returns in four starts against Spurs. Also proving popular is Pedro Neto (£6.5m) following his 15-point return last time out. The Portugal international scored twice and notched maximum bonus points. He was the highest-scoring player in the game in GW7. Neto has had four big chances, putting him second among all Blues players. Over 130,000 managers have purchased the right-wing back. With Bukayo Saka flagged as an injury doubt, Cole Palmer (£9.7m) will no doubt be in demand as the deadline approaches. The Chelsea number 10 is averaging just under six points per match in 26/27 and is yet to blank at Stamford Bridge, picking up a goal and three assists at home. Josh Acheampong (£4.5m) has started each of the last two Gameweeks and played his part in the Blues’ first clean sheet of the season. The England under-21 international picked up defensive contribution points against Everton, the second time he has reached the threshold in four starts. At just £4.5m, Acheampong has the potential to provide very good value in your FPL defence. In goal, Mike Penders (£4.4m) looks set to start with Emi Martinez (£5.0m) undergoing surgery for a fractured jaw. If selected, the Belgian will be the cheapest starting goalkeeper in the entire game. Spurs have scored just once in three away matches so far this season. Outside of Chelsea players, Erling Haaland (£15.7m) is a reliable captaincy option for Man City’s Saturday lunchtime trip to Aston Villa. The Norwegian has scored in six consecutive Gameweeks with eight goals, two double-digit hauls, 12 bonus points and 56 Fantasy points in that time. Haaland has been passed fit in the pre-Gameweek press conference. No player has had more shots on target or xGI than the league’s top scorer. Elsewhere, Morgan Gibbs-White (£7.9m) is an intriguing, differential option against Ipswich Town. Oliver Glasner confirmed in his press conference on Wednesday that the Nottingham Forest talisman is fit and available after missing GW7 with a knock. No player has created more big chances than Gibbs-White (7), who has picked up three attacking returns in three away matches. Opponents Ipswich are yet to keep a clean sheet so far this season.
